settings.type: string, one of the aliases "fable", "opus", or "sonnet", which resolve to Claude Code's current default version of that model family, or a full model ID such as "claude-opus-5-5"
settings.default: unset, so the advisor is off

description.en: Pick which model answers when Claude calls the server-side advisor tool. Unset it to turn the advisor off. The advisor must be at least as capable as your main model. See Choose an advisor model for the accepted pairings and what happens when you pick one that isn't accepted.
description.zh: Pick which model answers when Claude calls the server-side advisor tool. Unset it to turn the advisor off. The advisor must be at least as capable as your main model. See Choose an advisor model for the accepted pairings and what happens when you pick one that isn't accepted.

settings.type: string, the name of a built-in or custom agent
settings.default: unset, so the main thread runs as Claude Code's default agent

description.en: Run the main thread as a named subagent, so Claude Code applies that subagent's system prompt, tool restrictions, and model to your session. The same key sets the default agent for sessions you dispatch from claude agents.
description.zh: Run the main thread as a named subagent, so Claude Code applies that subagent's system prompt, tool restrictions, and model to your session. The same key sets the default agent for sessions you dispatch from claude agents.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code also reads a value left in ~/.claude.json by older versions.
settings.default: false

description.en: Allow Claude to send a push notification to your phone when it decides one is worth sending, for example when a long task finishes. Claude Code syncs this choice to your account, and pushes arrive while Remote Control is connected. Appears in /config as Push when Claude decides.
description.zh: Allow Claude to send a push notification to your phone when it decides one is worth sending, for example when a long task finishes. Claude Code syncs this choice to your account, and pushes arrive while Remote Control is connected. Appears in /config as Push when Claude decides.

settings.scope: Managed. Users can't re-enable connectors that exclusive control suppressed.
settings.default: false, so a deployed managed-mcp.json suppresses the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself

description.en: Load the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json. Without this key, managed-mcp.json takes exclusive control of MCP servers and suppresses those connectors.
description.zh: Load the claude.ai connectors Claude Code fetches itself alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json. Without this key, managed-mcp.json takes exclusive control of MCP servers and suppresses those connectors.

settings.scope: Managed, from the device's own managed settings only: an MDM-deployed plist or HKLM registry key, or a system managed-settings.json file. Claude Code ignores it in server-managed settings, in the user-writable HKCU registry, and in user or project settings.
settings.default: false, so a deployed managed-mcp.json blocks Claude in Chrome in terminal sessions

description.en: Let the built-in Claude in Chrome server run alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json. Without this key, a deployed managed-mcp.json blocks Claude in Chrome in terminal sessions. Requires Claude Code v2.1.282 or later.
description.zh: Let the built-in Claude in Chrome server run alongside a deployed managed-mcp.json. Without this key, a deployed managed-mcp.json blocks Claude in Chrome in terminal sessions. Requires Claude Code v2.1.282 or later.

settings.type: array of objects, each with marketplace and plugin strings. An entry can instead be a "plugin@marketplace" string such as "telegram@claude-plugins-official", which Claude Code treats as the equivalent object. The string form requires Claude Code v2.1.267 or later; earlier versions reject the whole allowedChannelPlugins value when it contains one
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the default Anthropic allowlist

description.en: Choose which channel plugins can push messages into sessions in your organization. When you set it, Claude Code uses your list in place of the default Anthropic allowlist; each entry names a plugin and the marketplace it comes from.
description.zh: Choose which channel plugins can push messages into sessions in your organization. When you set it, Claude Code uses your list in place of the default Anthropic allowlist; each entry names a plugin and the marketplace it comes from.

settings.scope: Any file. Arrays merge across settings files.
settings.type: array of URL patterns, with * as a wildcard
settings.default: unset, so any URL is allowed

description.en: Limit which URLs HTTP hooks can target. When you define this key, Claude Code runs an HTTP hook only if its URL matches one of the patterns and blocks the rest without running them; an empty array blocks every HTTP hook.
description.zh: Limit which URLs HTTP hooks can target. When you define this key, Claude Code runs an HTTP hook only if its URL matches one of the patterns and blocks the rest without running them; an empty array blocks every HTTP hook.

settings.scope: Any file. Entries from every file merge into one allowlist unless allowManagedMcpServersOnly is set. Deploy it in managed settings to enforce it.
settings.type: array of objects, each with exactly one key: serverName, a string limited to letters, numbers, hyphens, and underscores; serverCommand, an array of the command and its arguments matched exactly; or serverUrl, a URL pattern with * wildcards
settings.default: unset, so every server is allowed; an empty array blocks every server users add

description.en: Allowlist the MCP servers people can add. Claude Code blocks any server that doesn't match an entry wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers a user passes with --mcp-config, and servers from claude.ai.
description.zh: Allowlist the MCP servers people can add. Claude Code blocks any server that doesn't match an entry wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers a user passes with --mcp-config, and servers from claude.ai.

settings.scope: Managed. A list that the machine's own admin sources set, MDM policies and managed settings files, keeps applying when server-managed settings also deliver one: a session may then use only the providers on both lists, so a server-managed list can narrow what the machine allows but never widen it. Which machine source's allowedProviders counts follows how Claude Code combines managed sources. A list delivered through server-managed settings alone reaches only the sessions that fetch server-managed settings.
settings.type: array of strings, each one of:
settings.default: unset, so any provider can be used

description.en: List the services a machine may reach Claude through, such as the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, or an LLM gateway. A session on a provider that isn't listed is refused at startup, at login, and when it next contacts the API, so switching to an unlisted provider mid-session is refused too. The refusal message names what selected the provider and the steps to continue. Requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later.
description.zh: List the services a machine may reach Claude through, such as the Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, or an LLM gateway. A session on a provider that isn't listed is refused at startup, at login, and when it next contacts the API, so switching to an unlisted provider mid-session is refused too. The refusal message names what selected the provider and the steps to continue. Requires Claude Code v2.1.285 or later.

settings.default: unset, so hooks from every settings scope and plugin run

description.en: Restrict hook execution to hooks your organization deploys.
description.zh: Restrict hook execution to hooks your organization deploys.

settings.default: false, so allowlists from every settings scope merge

description.en: Make the managed allowlist the only one that applies. Claude Code then reads allowedMcpServers from managed settings alone and ignores allowlists in user, project, and local settings; deniedMcpServers still merges from every settings scope, so users can still block servers for themselves. Administrators set it so a user's own settings can't broaden what the managed allowlist permits.
description.zh: Make the managed allowlist the only one that applies. Claude Code then reads allowedMcpServers from managed settings alone and ignores allowlists in user, project, and local settings; deniedMcpServers still merges from every settings scope, so users can still block servers for themselves. Administrators set it so a user's own settings can't broaden what the managed allowlist permits.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code applies permission rules from user, project, and local settings and from --settings, in addition to the managed ones

description.en: Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules. Claude Code then ignores allow, ask, and deny rules in user, project, local, and --settings files, ignores --allowedTools, hides the always-allow choices in permission prompts, and stops saving new rules.
description.zh: Make managed settings the only settings source of permission rules. Claude Code then ignores allow, ask, and deny rules in user, project, local, and --settings files, ignores --allowedTools, hides the always-allow choices in permission prompts, and stops saving new rules.

settings.default: unset, so thinking is on for models that support it

description.en: Turn extended thinking off for every session by setting this to false. Thinking is on by default, so true changes nothing. Most people set this through /config rather than by editing the file.
description.zh: Turn extended thinking off for every session by setting this to false. Thinking is on by default, so true changes nothing. Most people set this through /config rather than by editing the file.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code doesn't run a helper

description.en: Run your own command to produce the credential Claude Code sends with model requests. Claude Code runs the command through the system shell, /bin/sh on macOS and Linux and cmd on Windows, and sends its output as both the X-Api-Key and Authorization: Bearer headers. Use it for dynamic or rotating credentials, such as short-lived tokens fetched from a vault.
description.zh: Run your own command to produce the credential Claude Code sends with model requests. Claude Code runs the command through the system shell, /bin/sh on macOS and Linux and cmd on Windows, and sends its output as both the X-Api-Key and Authorization: Bearer headers. Use it for dynamic or rotating credentials, such as short-lived tokens fetched from a vault.

settings.scope: User or managed. Claude Code reads the key from managed settings. It reads the key from user settings only on a machine with no managed settings, for a user who isn't signed in with a Team or Enterprise plan. It ignores the key in project and local settings and in a --settings file.
settings.default: unset

description.en: List the managed plugins whose mods run after every mod a user installs, in the listed order. An id listed in both prependPlugins and appendPlugins is prepended. In managed settings, Claude Code skips an id whose plugin doesn't count as your organization's.
description.zh: List the managed plugins whose mods run after every mod a user installs, in the listed order. An id listed in both prependPlugins and appendPlugins is prepended. In managed settings, Claude Code skips an id whose plugin doesn't count as your organization's.

settings.default: "never"

description.en: Let an unanswered AskUserQuestion dialog auto-continue after a period of idle time, submitting whatever options you had already selected. Set it when you step away and want Claude to continue without you. With the default, questions wait until you answer them. For when the timer pauses or never starts, see Question auto-continue timeout.
description.zh: Let an unanswered AskUserQuestion dialog auto-continue after a period of idle time, submitting whatever options you had already selected. Set it when you step away and want Claude to continue without you. With the default, questions wait until you answer them. For when the timer pauses or never starts, see Question auto-continue timeout.

settings.type: object with commit and pr strings and a sessionUrl Boolean, or false to hide all attribution. The false value requires Claude Code v2.1.281 or later; earlier versions reject it and skip the whole user, project, or local settings file that holds it
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the standard attribution shown under each sub-key

description.en: Customize the attribution Claude Code adds to git commits and pull requests. Commits get a git trailer such as Co-Authored-By by default; pull request descriptions get plain text. Set each part separately with the sub-keys below.
description.zh: Customize the attribution Claude Code adds to git commits and pull requests. Commits get a git trailer such as Co-Authored-By by default; pull request descriptions get plain text. Set each part separately with the sub-keys below.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code adds Co-Authored-By: . The name is the model in use when the commit is made, such as Claude Sonnet 5. When a subagent makes the commit, the trailer names the subagent's model.

description.en: Set the attribution text Claude Code adds to git commits, including any trailers. Set it to an empty string to hide commit attribution.
description.zh: Set the attribution text Claude Code adds to git commits, including any trailers. Set it to an empty string to hide commit attribution.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code adds 🤖 Generated with Claude Code

description.en: Set the attribution text Claude Code adds to pull request descriptions. Set it to an empty string to hide pull request attribution.
description.zh: Set the attribution text Claude Code adds to pull request descriptions. Set it to an empty string to hide pull request attribution.

settings.default: true

description.en: Choose whether Claude Code appends the claude.ai session link when it commits or opens a pull request from a cloud or Remote Control session. Claude Code adds the link as a Claude-Session trailer on commits and as a link in pull request descriptions. Set it to false to omit the link.
description.zh: Choose whether Claude Code appends the claude.ai session link when it commits or opens a pull request from a cloud or Remote Control session. Claude Code adds the link as a Claude-Session trailer on commits and as a link in pull request descriptions. Set it to false to omit the link.

settings.default: true

description.en: Have Claude Code compact the conversation automatically when context approaches the limit. Appears in /config as Auto-compact, and toggling it there writes this key to your user settings.
description.zh: Have Claude Code compact the conversation automatically when context approaches the limit. Appears in /config as Auto-compact, and toggling it there writes this key to your user settings.

settings.type: number of tokens, from 100000 to 1000000. Claude Code caps the value at your model's context window; the models overview lists each model's window
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code picks a window tuned for your model

description.en: Set how full the context window gets before Claude Code compacts automatically.
description.zh: Set how full the context window gets before Claude Code compacts automatically.

settings.scope: User or managed. Read from user settings, --settings, and managed settings only. When none of those sets the key, a project or local settings file that sets it turns the feature off rather than being ignored.
settings.default: true

description.en: After a claude.ai usage limit stops your session, wait in the open session and continue the task automatically after the reset. See Turn automatic continue off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later.
description.zh: After a claude.ai usage limit stops your session, wait in the open session and continue the task automatically after the reset. See Turn automatic continue off. Requires Claude Code v2.1.234 or later.

settings.type: string, an absolute or ~/-prefixed directory path
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses ~/.claude/projects//memory/

description.en: Store auto memory in a directory of your choice instead of the per-project default.
description.zh: Store auto memory in a directory of your choice instead of the per-project default.

settings.default: true

description.en: Turn auto memory on or off. When false, Claude doesn't read from or write to the auto memory directory. You can also toggle it with /memory during a session, which writes this key to your user settings.
description.zh: Turn auto memory on or off. When false, Claude doesn't read from or write to the auto memory directory. You can also toggle it with /memory during a session, which writes this key to your user settings.

settings.type: object with environment, allow, soft_deny, and hard_deny arrays of prose rules, plus the classifyAllShell Boolean
settings.default: unset, so the classifier uses only its built-in rules

description.en: Add your own rules to what the auto mode classifier blocks and allows. Use it to tell the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains your organization trusts, so it stops blocking routine internal operations. The classifier ships with built-in allow and deny rules. Include the literal string "$defaults" in an array to keep those built-in rules at that position and add yours around them; leave it out to replace them with yours.
description.zh: Add your own rules to what the auto mode classifier blocks and allows. Use it to tell the classifier which repos, buckets, and domains your organization trusts, so it stops blocking routine internal operations. The classifier ships with built-in allow and deny rules. Include the literal string "$defaults" in an array to keep those built-in rules at that position and add yours around them; leave it out to replace them with yours.

settings.scope: User or managed. Read wherever autoMode is read.
settings.default: false

description.en: Send every Bash and PowerShell command through the auto mode classifier while auto mode is active. By default, auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code: tool-wide and wildcard rules such as Bash(), and interpreter or shell-wrapper prefixes such as Bash(python ). A command that any other allow rule matches, such as Bash(npm test), skips the classifier unless it carries per-command allowed domains. When it skips, a destructive argument the rule's prefix didn't anticipate can get through unseen. Setting this key suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every command. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.
description.zh: Send every Bash and PowerShell command through the auto mode classifier while auto mode is active. By default, auto mode suspends only allow rules that could run arbitrary code: tool-wide and wildcard rules such as Bash(), and interpreter or shell-wrapper prefixes such as Bash(python ). A command that any other allow rule matches, such as Bash(npm test), skips the classifier unless it carries per-command allowed domains. When it skips, a destructive argument the rule's prefix didn't anticipate can get through unseen. Setting this key suspends every shell allow rule for the session so the classifier sees every command. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.

settings.default: true

description.en: Follow new output to the bottom of the conversation in fullscreen rendering. Turn it off to stay where you scrolled while Claude keeps working; permission prompts still scroll into view.
description.zh: Follow new output to the bottom of the conversation in fullscreen rendering. Turn it off to stay where you scrolled while Claude keeps working; permission prompts still scroll into view.

settings.scope: Any file. Set it in managed settings to enforce one channel across your organization.
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code follows "latest"

description.en: Choose which release channel background auto-updates and claude update follow. Set "stable" for a version that is typically about one week old and skips releases with major regressions, or "latest" for the most recent release.
description.zh: Choose which release channel background auto-updates and claude update follow. Set "stable" for a version that is typically about one week old and skips releases with major regressions, or "latest" for the most recent release.

settings.scope: Any file. Deploy it in managed settings to enforce it for an organization.
settings.type: array of model aliases or IDs
settings.default: unset, so every model is available

description.en: Restrict which models people can select for the main session, subagents, skills, and the advisor. A managed list constrains /model, --model, and the model key in a developer's own files; a model outside it can't be selected. With the default prefix matching, this doesn't touch the Default option on its own; pair it with enforceAvailableModels for that.
description.zh: Restrict which models people can select for the main session, subagents, skills, and the advisor. A managed list constrains /model, --model, and the model key in a developer's own files; a model outside it can't be selected. With the default prefix matching, this doesn't touch the Default option on its own; pair it with enforceAvailableModels for that.

settings.scope: Managed. Claude Code ignores the key in user, project, and local settings and in --settings, with a warning
settings.default: "prefix"

description.en: Choose how availableModels entries match model IDs. By default a model ID entry also permits later versions that extend it, so "claude-opus-5" permits Opus 5.5. With "exact", each model ID entry permits only the version it names, so a newer version of that model stays blocked until you list it. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.
description.zh: Choose how availableModels entries match model IDs. By default a model ID entry also permits later versions that extend it, so "claude-opus-5" permits Opus 5.5. With "exact", each model ID entry permits only the version it names, so a newer version of that model stays blocked until you list it. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.

settings.default: unset, so the recap is on

description.en: Show a one-line session recap when you return to the terminal after a few minutes away. Set it to false, or turn off Session recap in /config, to stop the recap.
description.zh: Show a one-line session recap when you return to the terminal after a few minutes away. Set it to false, or turn off Session recap in /config, to stop the recap.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code doesn't refresh AWS credentials for you

description.en: Run your own command, such as aws sso login, to refresh the credentials in your .aws directory when the ones Claude Code has for Amazon Bedrock stop working. Claude Code checks the current credentials against STS first and runs the command only when that check fails, then reads the refreshed .aws directory.
description.zh: Run your own command, such as aws sso login, to refresh the credentials in your .aws directory when the ones Claude Code has for Amazon Bedrock stop working. Claude Code checks the current credentials against STS first and runs the command only when that check fails, then reads the refreshed .aws directory.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the ambient AWS credential chain

description.en: Run your own command that prints AWS credentials as JSON, so Claude Code can call Amazon Bedrock with credentials that don't live in your .aws directory. Claude Code accepts the aws sts output shape and the flat aws configure export-credentials shape, and scopes the credentials to its own Bedrock client, so the shell commands Claude runs still see your ambient credentials.
description.zh: Run your own command that prints AWS credentials as JSON, so Claude Code can call Amazon Bedrock with credentials that don't live in your .aws directory. Claude Code accepts the aws sts output shape and the flat aws configure export-credentials shape, and scopes the credentials to its own Bedrock client, so the shell commands Claude runs still see your ambient credentials.

settings.default: unset, so screen-reader mode is off

description.en: Render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Screen-reader mode uses the classic renderer, so the tui setting has no effect while it is active; attached background sessions still render fullscreen.
description.zh: Render screen-reader friendly output: flat text without decorative borders or animations. Screen-reader mode uses the classic renderer, so the tui setting has no effect while it is active; attached background sessions still render fullscreen.

settings.scope: User or managed. A true counts only from your user settings, JSON passed with --settings, or managed settings, so a true in a repository's .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json can't turn the recording on. A false in either repository file still turns it off unless a higher-precedence file sets true.
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code records changes in auto mode and bypassPermissions mode when it directs Claude to edit files through Bash

description.en: Choose whether Claude Code records which files changed in a Git repository while a Bash command runs. When it records them, you see their diff in the terminal after the command, and your PostToolUse Bash hooks receive the changed-file list.
description.zh: Choose whether Claude Code records which files changed in a Git repository while a Bash command runs. When it records them, you see their diff in the terminal after the command, and your PostToolUse Bash hooks receive the changed-file list.

settings.type: number of characters, a positive integer. Claude Code clamps the value into the range 4000 to 128000
settings.default: unset, so Claude receives up to 30,000 characters inline

description.en: Set how many characters of a successful Bash or PowerShell command's output Claude receives inline. When output passes the limit, Claude Code saves it to a file and Claude receives a short preview plus the file's path. Raise the limit when command output, such as a verbose build or a full test-suite log, routinely overflows the default and you want Claude to read it without opening the file. Requires Claude Code v2.1.261 or later.
description.zh: Set how many characters of a successful Bash or PowerShell command's output Claude receives inline. When output passes the limit, Claude Code saves it to a file and Claude receives a short preview plus the file's path. Raise the limit when command output, such as a verbose build or a full test-suite log, routinely overflows the default and you want Claude to read it without opening the file. Requires Claude Code v2.1.261 or later.

settings.type: array of marketplace source objects, in the same forms as strictKnownMarketplaces
settings.default: unset, so no marketplace is blocked

description.en: Block plugin marketplace sources for your organization. Claude Code checks the blocklist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins either. Blocked sources are checked before download, so they never touch the filesystem.
description.zh: Block plugin marketplace sources for your organization. Claude Code checks the blocklist on marketplace add and on plugin install, update, refresh, and auto-update, so a marketplace someone added before you set the policy can't be used to fetch plugins either. Blocked sources are checked before download, so they never touch the filesystem.

settings.type: string, "disabled"; the desktop app also accepts "disable", in either case
settings.default: unset, so Claude's tools work on external pages

description.en: Stop Claude from using its tools to read or act on external pages in the desktop app's Browser pane. People in your organization can still open external sites themselves, and local dev server previews keep working with Claude's tools. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.
description.zh: Stop Claude from using its tools to read or act on external pages in the desktop app's Browser pane. People in your organization can still open external sites themselves, and local dev server previews keep working with Claude's tools. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.

settings.default: unset; channels are blocked on Team and Enterprise plans and on Console accounts with managed settings, and allowed on Pro and Max plans and on Console accounts without managed settings

description.en: Allow channels for your organization. On claude.ai Team and Enterprise plans, Claude Code blocks channels until you set this to true. For Anthropic Console accounts that authenticate with an API key, channels are allowed by default. If your organization deploys managed settings, Claude Code blocks channels on those accounts too until you set this key to true.
description.zh: Allow channels for your organization. On claude.ai Team and Enterprise plans, Claude Code blocks channels until you set this to true. For Anthropic Console accounts that authenticate with an API key, channels are allowed by default. If your organization deploys managed settings, Claude Code blocks channels on those accounts too until you set this key to true.

settings.type: string, the text of a CLAUDE.md file; write it as you would the file, Markdown included, with line breaks as \n
settings.default: unset

description.en: Inject CLAUDE.md-style instructions as organization-managed memory without deploying a separate file. Claude Code loads the text as a managed memory entry ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md files.
description.zh: Inject CLAUDE.md-style instructions as organization-managed memory without deploying a separate file. Claude Code loads the text as a managed memory entry ahead of user and project CLAUDE.md files.

settings.type: array of strings, each a glob pattern or absolute path
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code loads every CLAUDE.md it finds

description.en: Skip specific CLAUDE.md files when Claude Code loads memory. In a large monorepo, use it to skip CLAUDE.md files from other teams that aren't relevant to your work; Exclude irrelevant CLAUDE.md files in the large-codebases guide walks through that case. Patterns match against absolute file paths.
description.zh: Skip specific CLAUDE.md files when Claude Code loads memory. In a large monorepo, use it to skip CLAUDE.md files from other teams that aren't relevant to your work; Exclude irrelevant CLAUDE.md files in the large-codebases guide walks through that case. Patterns match against absolute file paths.

settings.type: number of days, a whole number, minimum 1

description.en: Set how many days Claude Code keeps session transcripts and other application data before deleting them. Claude Code runs the deletion as a background sweep after a session starts, as long as it can safely determine the retention period. The sweep deletes transcripts without showing a message, so a session you haven't used for longer than the retention period no longer appears in the /resume picker.
description.zh: Set how many days Claude Code keeps session transcripts and other application data before deleting them. Claude Code runs the deletion as a background sweep after a session starts, as long as it can safely determine the retention period. The sweep deletes transcripts without showing a message, so a session you haven't used for longer than the retention period no longer appears in the /resume picker.

settings.default: unset, so no announcement shows

description.en: Show your organization's announcements to users at startup. When you list more than one, Claude Code picks one at random for each session; on a person's very first launch it shows the first entry.
description.zh: Show your organization's announcements to users at startup. When you list more than one, Claude Code picks one at random for each session; on a person's very first launch it shows the first entry.

settings.scope: Any file. A project or local value applies only when it's stricter than the value managed settings, the --settings flag, or user settings give.
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code decides per message

description.en: Choose what this session does with messages arriving from your other Claude Code sessions. When no value applies, Claude Code decides per message from the two sessions' permission-mode classes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
description.zh: Choose what this session does with messages arriving from your other Claude Code sessions. When no value applies, Claude Code decides per message from the two sessions' permission-mode classes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

settings.default: "bash", or "powershell" on Windows when Bash isn't available

description.en: Choose whether Bash or PowerShell runs the shell commands you type with the ! prefix in the input box, the ones Claude Code runs directly and adds to the session.
description.zh: Choose whether Bash or PowerShell runs the shell commands you type with the ! prefix in the input box, the ones Claude Code runs directly and adds to the session.

settings.scope: Any file. Entries from every file merge into one denylist, and allowManagedMcpServersOnly doesn't change that. Deploy it in managed settings to enforce it.
settings.type: array of objects, each with exactly one key: serverName, a string, so a claude.ai connector's display name such as "claude.ai Slack" works; serverCommand, an array of the command and its arguments matched exactly; or serverUrl, a URL pattern with * wildcards
settings.default: unset, so no server is blocked; an empty array also blocks nothing

description.en: Block specific MCP servers. Claude Code refuses to load a matching server wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers passed with --mcp-config, servers from managed-mcp.json, servers from managedMcpServers, and the claude.ai connectors it fetches itself. In-process type: "sdk" servers are exempt; the app that started the session registers them.
description.zh: Block specific MCP servers. Claude Code refuses to load a matching server wherever it's defined, including plugin servers, servers passed with --mcp-config, servers from managed-mcp.json, servers from managedMcpServers, and the claude.ai connectors it fetches itself. In-process type: "sdk" servers are exempt; the app that started the session registers them.

settings.scope: Managed. Claude Code ignores the key in user, project, and local settings and in --settings, with a warning
settings.type: array of model aliases or IDs
settings.default: unset, so no model is blocked

description.en: Block specific models, with or without an availableModels allowlist and even when that list permits them. Claude Code hides a blocked model from the /model picker, and the model can't be selected anywhere availableModels is enforced. A session on the Default option doesn't run a blocked model either, as Block specific models or versions describes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.
description.zh: Block specific models, with or without an availableModels allowlist and even when that list permits them. A session on the Default option doesn't run a blocked model either, as Block specific models or versions describes. Requires Claude Code v2.1.283 or later.

settings.scope: User or managed. Claude Code also reads the key from a file you pass with --settings, and ignores it in project and local settings.
settings.type: number of days, a whole number, minimum 0
settings.default: 0, which sets no age limit

description.en: Set an age limit in days for the transcripts of sessions you started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork. Without this key, Claude Code keeps those transcripts at any age. Claude Code deletes each one once it's older than both this limit and cleanupPeriodDays, so with cleanupPeriodDays at its default of 30, a value of 7 still keeps them 30 days. Cleaned up automatically lists the cases where cleanupPeriodDays applies instead and Claude Code ignores this key. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.
description.zh: Set an age limit in days for the transcripts of sessions you started or most recently continued in Claude Desktop or Cowork. Without this key, Claude Code keeps those transcripts at any age. Claude Code deletes each one once it's older than both this limit and cleanupPeriodDays, so with cleanupPeriodDays at its default of 30, a value of 7 still keeps them 30 days. Cleaned up automatically lists the cases where cleanupPeriodDays applies instead and Claude Code ignores this key. Requires Claude Code v2.1.248 or later.

settings.type: string, one of "60s", "5m", "10m", or "never", which disables the deadline

description.en: Set the deadline for dialogs Claude Code forwards to a remote client, such as a Remote Control or SDK host, and for the approval dialog for a held cross-session message. On Claude Code v2.1.236 or later, the same deadline bounds the mid-session Fable usage-credits consent prompt in a session that may have nobody at the terminal. When no answer arrives before the deadline, Claude Code cancels the dialog and continues with its no-action default. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.
description.zh: Set the deadline for dialogs Claude Code forwards to a remote client, such as a Remote Control or SDK host, and for the approval dialog for a held cross-session message. On Claude Code v2.1.236 or later, the same deadline bounds the mid-session Fable usage-credits consent prompt in a session that may have nobody at the terminal. When no answer arrives before the deadline, Claude Code cancels the dialog and continues with its no-action default. Requires Claude Code v2.1.224 or later.

settings.default: unset, so agent view is available

description.en: Turn off background agents and agent view: claude agents, --bg, /background, and the on-demand supervisor. Set it in managed settings to enforce it for an organization.
description.zh: Turn off background agents and agent view: claude agents, --bg, /background, and the on-demand supervisor. Set it in managed settings to enforce it for an organization.

settings.scope: Any file. Only managed settings can disable managed hooks.
settings.default: unset, so hooks run

description.en: Turn off hooks, any custom status line, and any custom file suggestion command. Use it to turn all of these off temporarily without deleting them from your settings.
description.zh: Turn off hooks, any custom status line, and any custom file suggestion command. Use it to turn all of these off temporarily without deleting them from your settings.

settings.default: unset, so the tool follows your account's availability

description.en: Use enableArtifact instead to turn off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the Artifacts row off in /config, Claude Code writes enableArtifact to your user settings and clears this key.
description.zh: Use enableArtifact instead to turn off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the Artifacts row off in /config, Claude Code writes enableArtifact to your user settings and clears this key.

settings.scope: Any file. Most useful in managed settings, where users can't override it. Also accepted under permissions as permissions.disableAutoMode.
settings.default: unset

description.en: Remove auto mode from the Shift+Tab cycle. Any session that would otherwise start in auto mode, whether from --permission-mode auto, a settings file, or the built-in default, starts in default instead. Administrators set it in managed settings to prevent developers in their organization from using auto mode.
description.zh: Remove auto mode from the Shift+Tab cycle. Any session that would otherwise start in auto mode, whether from --permission-mode auto, a settings file, or the built-in default, starts in default instead. Administrators set it in managed settings to prevent developers in their organization from using auto mode.

settings.type: Boolean; only the JSON Boolean true takes effect
settings.default: unset, so external browsing is on

description.en: Turn off external browsing in the desktop app's Browser pane for people and Claude alike. Localhost dev server previews keep working. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.
description.zh: Turn off external browsing in the desktop app's Browser pane for people and Claude alike. Localhost dev server previews keep working. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.

settings.default: unset, so bundled skills load

description.en: Turn off the skills and workflows included with Claude Code. Claude Code removes bundled skills and workflows entirely, while built-in commands such as /init stay typable but are hidden from the model.
description.zh: Turn off the skills and workflows included with Claude Code. Claude Code removes bundled skills and workflows entirely, while built-in commands such as /init stay typable but are hidden from the model.

settings.default: false, so Claude Code fetches your connectors

description.en: Turn off the claude.ai MCP connectors Claude Code fetches itself, so it neither fetches nor connects them. A true in any settings file applies: a checked-in project .claude/settings.json can opt a repository out of those connectors, but a project-level false can't override a user- or managed-level true.
description.zh: Turn off the claude.ai MCP connectors Claude Code fetches itself, so it neither fetches nor connects them. A true in any settings file applies: a checked-in project .claude/settings.json can opt a repository out of those connectors, but a project-level false can't override a user- or managed-level true.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code follows allowManagedHooksOnly: an organization that restricts hook execution to managed settings gets command sources disabled too

description.en: Block the command plugin source, which installs a plugin by running a marketplace-declared command on the user's machine. When you set it to true, Claude Code never runs the command, doesn't install or update command-sourced plugins, and stops loading the ones already installed. Set it to false to allow them explicitly. Whenever it blocks command sources, whether you set it to true or leave it unset under allowManagedHooksOnly, it also blocks marketplace headersHelper commands, except for a marketplace that managed settings themselves declare. Requires Claude Code v2.1.229 or later, and the headersHelper block requires v2.1.238 or later.
description.zh: Block the command plugin source, which installs a plugin by running a marketplace-declared command on the user's machine. Requires Claude Code v2.1.229 or later, and the headersHelper block requires v2.1.238 or later.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code registers the handler

description.en: Stop Claude Code from registering the claude-cli:// protocol handler with the operating system, which it otherwise does after you send the first prompt of an interactive session. Deep links let external tools open a Claude Code session with a pre-filled prompt. Set this in environments where protocol handler registration is restricted or managed separately.
description.zh: Stop Claude Code from registering the claude-cli:// protocol handler with the operating system, which it otherwise does after you send the first prompt of an interactive session. Deep links let external tools open a Claude Code session with a pre-filled prompt. Set this in environments where protocol handler registration is restricted or managed separately.

settings.scope: Managed. By default, the desktop app reads the key from one managed source.
settings.type: Boolean; only the JSON Boolean true takes effect
settings.default: unset, so local sessions are available

description.en: Turn off Code sessions that run on the device in the desktop app, for deployments where developers should work on remote machines over SSH. In the Code tab, the Local environment stays in the environment dropdown but is grayed out and can't be selected, with a tooltip saying your organization turned it off; on Windows the WSL entry is grayed out the same way, though whether WSL sessions run on a managed device at all is governed separately. New sessions default to the first SSH connection if one is configured, and the app refuses to start or resume a session on the device, including an SSH connection back to the same machine. SSH sessions to other hosts and cloud sessions are unaffected. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.37937.0 or later.
description.zh: Turn off Code sessions that run on the device in the desktop app, for deployments where developers should work on remote machines over SSH. In the Code tab, the Local environment stays in the environment dropdown but is grayed out and can't be selected, with a tooltip saying your organization turned it off; on Windows the WSL entry is grayed out the same way, though whether WSL sessions run on a managed device at all is governed separately. New sessions default to the first SSH connection if one is configured, and the app refuses to start or resume a session on the device, including an SSH connection back to the same machine. SSH sessions to other hosts and cloud sessions are unaffected. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.37937.0 or later.

settings.type: array of strings, the server names as they appear in .mcp.json
settings.default: unset

description.en: Reject specific servers defined in a project's .mcp.json file so Claude Code never connects them or asks you to approve them. A rejection in any settings file applies, including a project .claude/settings.json checked into the repository.
description.zh: Reject specific servers defined in a project's .mcp.json file so Claude Code never connects them or asks you to approve them. A rejection in any settings file applies, including a project .claude/settings.json checked into the repository.

settings.type: Boolean; only the JSON Boolean true takes effect
settings.default: unset, so Claude's simulator tools follow each person's settings toggle in the desktop app

description.en: Block Claude's tools for the desktop app's iOS Simulator pane. People keep manual use of the pane; only Claude's access is removed, and nobody can turn it back on from inside the app. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.
description.zh: Block Claude's tools for the desktop app's iOS Simulator pane. People keep manual use of the pane; only Claude's access is removed, and nobody can turn it back on from inside the app. The desktop app reads this key; the terminal CLI ignores it.

settings.default: false

description.en: Turn off Remote Control: Claude Code then refuses claude remote-control, the --remote-control flag, auto-start, and the in-session toggle, and reports that your organization's policy disabled it. Place it in managed settings for per-device MDM enforcement.
description.zh: Turn off Remote Control: Claude Code then refuses claude remote-control, the --remote-control flag, auto-start, and the in-session toggle, and reports that your organization's policy disabled it. Place it in managed settings for per-device MDM enforcement.

settings.default: false

description.en: Reject the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass strictKnownMarketplaces for a single run. Claude Code exits with an error naming the rejected flags. In cloud sessions, Claude Code instead starts the session and drops every server-delivered --mcp-config entry except in-process type: "sdk" entries and a Claude Tag session's Slack tools. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.
description.zh: Reject the --plugin-dir, --plugin-url, --agents, and --mcp-config CLI flags at startup, which users could otherwise pass to bypass strictKnownMarketplaces for a single run. Requires Claude Code v2.1.193 or later.

settings.scope: Any file. A true in managed settings can't be overridden by false elsewhere.
settings.default: unset, so inline shell runs

description.en: Turn off inline shell execution for ` !... and ``! blocks in skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or additional-directory sources. Claude Code replaces each command with [shell command execution disabled by policy] instead of running it.
description.zh: Turn off inline shell execution for ` !... and ``! blocks in skills and custom commands from user, project, plugin, or additional-directory sources. Claude Code replaces each command with [shell command execution disabled by policy] instead of running it.

settings.default: false

description.en: Turn off dynamic workflows and the bundled workflow commands for everyone your settings reach, such as an organization through managed settings. To turn workflows on or off just for yourself, use enableWorkflows instead, which the Dynamic workflows toggle in /config writes to your user settings.
description.zh: Turn off dynamic workflows and the bundled workflow commands for everyone your settings reach, such as an organization through managed settings. To turn workflows on or off just for yourself, use enableWorkflows instead, which the Dynamic workflows toggle in /config writes to your user settings.

settings.default: "normal"

description.en: Choose the key binding mode for the input prompt.
description.zh: Choose the key binding mode for the input prompt.

settings.default: unset

description.en: Set a default effort level for models you haven't saved a level for. Lower levels are faster and cheaper on straightforward tasks, and higher levels reason more deeply on complex problems.
description.zh: Set a default effort level for models you haven't saved a level for. Lower levels are faster and cheaper on straightforward tasks, and higher levels reason more deeply on complex problems.

settings.default: true

description.en: Show emoji suggestions when you type : plus a shortcode in the prompt input, and replace a completed shortcode such as :heart: with its emoji. Set it to false to turn off both.
description.zh: Show emoji suggestions when you type : plus a shortcode in the prompt input, and replace a completed shortcode such as :heart: with its emoji. Set it to false to turn off both.

settings.scope: Any file. In a folder whose trust dialog you haven't accepted, Claude Code honors it from user settings, managed settings, and --settings and ignores it in the shared project file, both in the session and for claude mcp list and claude mcp get; Project server approvals and workspace trust says when an untracked .claude/settings.local.json counts too.
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code asks you to approve each server

description.en: Approve every MCP server defined in project .mcp.json files without a prompt. Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you choose to approve all servers in the approval dialog.
description.zh: Approve every MCP server defined in project .mcp.json files without a prompt. Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you choose to approve all servers in the approval dialog.

settings.scope: Any file. Every file can turn the tool off, and none can turn it back on.
settings.default: unset, so the tool follows your account's availability

description.en: Turn off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the Artifacts row off in /config, Claude Code writes this key to your user settings, so you don't usually edit it by hand.
description.zh: Turn off the Artifact tool, which publishes session output as a private web page on claude.ai. When you turn the Artifacts row off in /config, Claude Code writes this key to your user settings, so you don't usually edit it by hand.

settings.type: array of strings, the server names as they appear in .mcp.json
settings.default: unset

description.en: Approve specific servers defined in project .mcp.json files so Claude Code connects them without asking. Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you approve a server in the approval dialog.
description.zh: Approve specific servers defined in project .mcp.json files so Claude Code connects them without asking. Claude Code writes this key to .claude/settings.local.json when you approve a server in the approval dialog.

settings.type: object mapping plugin-name@marketplace-name to a Boolean
settings.default: unset, so each plugin follows its defaultEnabled value

description.en: Turn individual plugins on or off, keyed by plugin-name@marketplace-name. A plugin with no entry at any scope falls back to its defaultEnabled value. When you enable or disable a plugin with /plugin or claude plugin enable, Claude Code writes this key for you.
description.zh: Turn individual plugins on or off, keyed by plugin-name@marketplace-name. A plugin with no entry at any scope falls back to its defaultEnabled value. When you enable or disable a plugin with /plugin or claude plugin enable, Claude Code writes this key for you.

settings.default: unset, so workflows are on unless you're on the Pro plan, where they're off

description.en: Turn dynamic workflows on or off for yourself when your plan's default isn't what you want. Appears in /config as Dynamic workflows, which writes this key to your user settings and removes it again when you toggle back to your plan's default. To turn workflows off for everyone from managed settings, use disableWorkflows instead.
description.zh: Turn dynamic workflows on or off for yourself when your plan's default isn't what you want. Appears in /config as Dynamic workflows, which writes this key to your user settings and removes it again when you toggle back to your plan's default. To turn workflows off for everyone from managed settings, use disableWorkflows instead.

settings.default: false

description.en: The /model picker has a Default option, and default model setting describes the model it resolves to. An availableModels allowlist limits the models you can name, but with the default prefix matching it doesn't remap your account type's default, so Default can still resolve to a model outside the list. This key closes that gap. Requires Claude Code v2.1.175 or later.
description.zh: The /model picker has a Default option, and default model setting describes the model it resolves to. An availableModels allowlist limits the models you can name, but with the default prefix matching it doesn't remap your account type's default, so Default can still resolve to a model outside the list. This key closes that gap. Requires Claude Code v2.1.175 or later.

settings.scope: Any file. Claude Code honors entries in a repository's .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json only after you accept the workspace trust dialog for that folder; in a folder you haven't trusted, including a -p run there, it ignores them without a message.
settings.type: object mapping a marketplace name to an object with a source object and an optional autoUpdate Boolean
settings.default: unset

description.en: Register additional plugin marketplaces by name, so that people who open the repository, or everyone your managed settings reach, get the marketplace without adding it themselves. Claude Code registers each marketplace it doesn't already know. Whether a plugin that enabledPlugins names from it installs depends on the plugin's source and which file enables it; that entry has the rules.
description.zh: Register additional plugin marketplaces by name, so that people who open the repository, or everyone your managed settings reach, get the marketplace without adding it themselves. Claude Code registers each marketplace it doesn't already know. Whether a plugin that enabledPlugins names from it installs depends on the plugin's source and which file enables it; that entry has the rules.

settings.type: array of model aliases or IDs; "default" expands to the default model
settings.default: unset, so a failed request isn't retried on another model

description.en: Name backup models for Claude Code to try, in order, when your primary model is overloaded or unavailable. Claude Code switches to the next available model in the chain for the rest of the turn and shows a notice. Without a chain, Claude Code retries the same model and then surfaces the server's error, and you retry or switch models yourself.
description.zh: Name backup models for Claude Code to try, in order, when your primary model is overloaded or unavailable. Claude Code switches to the next available model in the chain for the rest of the turn and shows a notice. Without a chain, Claude Code retries the same model and then surfaces the server's error, and you retry or switch models yourself.

settings.default: unset, so fast mode is off

description.en: Turn fast mode on for sessions where it's available, for interactive work like rapid iteration or live debugging where you want speed at a higher cost per token. You don't usually edit this key by hand: running /fast writes fastMode: true to ~/.claude/settings.json, and running it again to turn fast mode off removes the key. Fast mode runs only on Opus 5.5, Opus 5, and Opus 4.8: turning it on from another model switches you to Opus, and switching to an unsupported model turns it off. See Switch models while fast mode is on.
description.zh: Turn fast mode on for sessions where it's available, for interactive work like rapid iteration or live debugging where you want speed at a higher cost per token. You don't usually edit this key by hand: running /fast writes fastMode: true to ~/.claude/settings.json, and running it again to turn fast mode off removes the key. Fast mode runs only on Opus 5.5, Opus 5, and Opus 4.8: turning it on from another model switches you to Opus, and switching to an unsupported model turns it off. See Switch models while fast mode is on.

settings.default: false

description.en: Normally, running /fast saves fastMode to a person's user settings, so fast mode is on at the start of every later session. Set this key to true to stop that: a saved fastMode: true no longer turns fast mode on at session start, and each person has to run /fast in each session they want it. Claude Code leaves the fastMode key in their file, so turning this key off restores the old behavior.

settings.default: "notify"

description.en: Control Claude-drafted feedback: whether Claude can queue feedback drafts for you to review, and whether Claude Code shows a card when Claude queues one.
description.zh: Control Claude-drafted feedback: whether Claude can queue feedback drafts for you to review, and whether Claude Code shows a card when Claude queues one.

settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the rate Anthropic sets remotely, or its built-in rate of 0.005 on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform, and Microsoft Foundry, which don't receive remote configuration

description.en: Set the probability that the session quality survey appears when a session is eligible for it. Set 0 to keep the survey from appearing.
description.zh: Set the probability that the session quality survey appears when a session is eligible for it. Set 0 to keep the survey from appearing.

settings.default: true

description.en: Have Claude Code snapshot files before each edit so /rewind can restore them. Appears in /config as Rewind code (checkpoints), and toggling it there writes this key to your user settings.
description.zh: Have Claude Code snapshot files before each edit so /rewind can restore them. Appears in /config as Rewind code (checkpoints), and toggling it there writes this key to your user settings.

settings.scope: Any file. Under the status line and file suggestion gates, Claude Code turns the command off or runs only a managed value, and skips yours without warning.
settings.type: object with type, always "command", and command, the shell command to run
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code uses the built-in file suggestion

description.en: Run your own command to supply @ file path autocomplete instead of the built-in file suggestion. The built-in suggestion uses fast filesystem traversal; a large monorepo may do better with project-specific indexing such as a pre-built file index.
description.zh: Run your own command to supply @ file path autocomplete instead of the built-in file suggestion. The built-in suggestion uses fast filesystem traversal; a large monorepo may do better with project-specific indexing such as a pre-built file index.

settings.type: array of objects, each with type set to "regex", a pattern regex, a url template, and an optional label; {name} placeholders in url and label are filled from named capture groups in pattern
settings.default: unset, so no badges render

description.en: Render extra clickable badges in the footer below the input box when a regex matches turn output: tool results, including file contents and fetched pages, and Claude's own responses. Use it to turn IDs printed by project CLIs, such as review tools and issue trackers, into session links.
description.zh: Render extra clickable badges in the footer below the input box when a regex matches turn output: tool results, including file contents and fetched pages, and Claude's own responses.
