Choose "small" when you want to bound what a workflow spends. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later.

settings.type: object with baseRef, symlinkDirectories, sparsePaths, and bgIsolation
settings.default: unset

description.en: Configure how Claude Code creates and manages git worktrees for --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, and isolated subagents and background sessions.
description.zh: Configure how Claude Code creates and manages git worktrees for --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, and isolated subagents and background sessions.

settings.default: "fresh"

description.en: Choose which ref new worktrees branch from. "fresh" branches from origin/ for a clean tree matching the remote; "head" branches from your current local HEAD, so unpushed commits and feature-branch state are present in the worktree.
description.zh: Choose which ref new worktrees branch from. "fresh" branches from origin/ for a clean tree matching the remote; "head" branches from your current local HEAD, so unpushed commits and feature-branch state are present in the worktree.

settings.default: "worktree"

description.en: Choose how background sessions isolate their file edits. If you moved a session to the background with ← or /background, that session edits files in place whatever this key says. With "worktree", Claude Code blocks Edit and Write in the main checkout until the session calls EnterWorktree; with "none", background jobs edit the working copy directly. Set "none" for a repository where git worktrees are impractical.
description.zh: Choose how background sessions isolate their file edits. If you moved a session to the background with ← or /background, that session edits files in place whatever this key says. With "worktree", Claude Code blocks Edit and Write in the main checkout until the session calls EnterWorktree; with "none", background jobs edit the working copy directly. Set "none" for a repository where git worktrees are impractical.

settings.scope: User, in ~/.claude/settings.json on the remote machine
settings.type: string, an absolute path or one that starts with ~/
settings.default: unset, so worktrees go inside the project

description.en: Choose the folder on a remote machine where Desktop SSH sessions create their worktrees, instead of /.claude/worktrees/. Only the desktop app reads this key: --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, isolated subagents, and background sessions ignore it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.44121.0 or later.
description.zh: Choose the folder on a remote machine where Desktop SSH sessions create their worktrees, instead of /.claude/worktrees/. Only the desktop app reads this key: --worktree, the EnterWorktree tool, isolated subagents, and background sessions ignore it. Requires Claude Desktop v1.44121.0 or later.

settings.type: array of strings, directory paths relative to the repository root
settings.default: unset, so each worktree checks out the whole tree

description.en: Check out only the listed directories in each worktree through git sparse-checkout. Claude Code writes only those directories plus root-level files to disk, which is faster in large monorepos; see Check out only the directories you need.
description.zh: Check out only the listed directories in each worktree through git sparse-checkout. Claude Code writes only those directories plus root-level files to disk, which is faster in large monorepos; see Check out only the directories you need.

settings.type: array of strings, directory paths relative to the repository root
settings.default: unset, so Claude Code symlinks no directories

description.en: Symlink directories from the main repository into each worktree so you don't duplicate large directories on disk.
description.zh: Symlink directories from the main repository into each worktree so you don't duplicate large directories on disk.

settings.scope: Managed. In an admin-controlled Windows source.
settings.default: false, so WSL reads only /etc/claude-code

description.en: Have Claude Code on WSL read managed settings from the Windows policy chain, with HKLM and the Windows managed settings file taking priority over /etc/claude-code and HKCU below it. While the chain is on, Claude Code reads /etc/claude-code only when no Windows admin document is present in the HKLM registry value or the C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\ folder. Set it to extend the policy you already deploy on Windows to WSL sessions on the same machine, so they follow the same rules as host sessions. Claude Code honors it only when set in the HKLM registry key or in a managed settings file or drop-in under C:\Program Files\ClaudeCode\, both of which require Windows admin to write.
